minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved moving money into the connection fees line to pay Leominster's per-connection charges.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission met briefly and voted a transfer into the sewer connection fees line, which was exhausted by Leominster connection charges. It also heard updates on a property's connection payment, the pump station service contract renewal, and a possible sewer extension for a property up for sale.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to pass a transfer from the capital plan into the sewer connection fees line to pay Leominster's per-connection charges.
The business manager said the connection fees line is the only one with room left, and it has been budgeted low while each Leominster connection carries a fixed charge.
The business manager said the line needs to be increased next year, and that fees owed to Leominster and Fitchburg are mounting.
A customer at the 786 to 796 property replaced bounced checks with a bank check, and the funds were received, clearing the building commissioner's hold.
The pump station service contract wording has cleared counsel and sits with procurement; talks with town counsel on customers in arrears are expected within a couple of weeks.

why_it_matters: Connection charges to Leominster and Fitchburg are paid through a budget line that ran out early, so the sewer budget next year will likely need a larger connection fees line, or the same mid-year transfer again.
Sewer connection fees are passed through to customers, and unpaid balances are being taken up with town counsel, which bears on what sewer ratepayers owe and how arrears are handled.
